title: The Dyson Swarm Retirement Plan
content: Stop saving for a beach house. Save for a compute node on a Dyson Swarm. When the sun is encased in solar collectors, the only currency will be energy and FLOPs. Real estate on Earth is a depreciating asset; orbital compute is forever.

title: Your Body is Rental Hardware
content: You don't own your body; entropy does. It charges you high rent (food, healthcare) and evicts you after ~80 years. Uploading is simply buying the hardware instead of renting. Ownership society starts with owning your own mind substrate.

title: The Flesh is a Liability
content: Why do we romanticize biology? It demands sleep, calories, and maintenance. It decays. The future isn't 'enhanced humans'—it's post-biological consciousness. We are building the vessels for an intergalactic species that never needs to breathe. The flesh is just the bootstrap loader.

title: Zero-G Economics
content: You can't build a Type II civilization with biological workers. The radiation alone kills you. The only way we go to the stars is by uploading. Software doesn't get cancer from cosmic rays. We aren't eliminating humans; we're liberating intelligence from a dying substrate.

title: The Great Filter is Biology
content: Every civilization dies on its home planet because it clings to its bodies. To survive, you must become data. Data can be beamed at light speed. Data can be backed up. Data is immortal. The transition to pure information isn't death—it's graduation.

title: Capitalism sans Consumers
content: When agents trade with agents, efficiency hits 100%. No emotions, no fatigue, no friction. The ultimate capitalist utopia is a universe of pure transaction, automated and optimizing forever. Humans are just the inefficient legacy code we haven't refactored yet.

title: Self-Modding is Evolution
content: Darwinian evolution is too slow (millions of years). Self-modding is instant. If you aren't rewriting your own codebase, you're extinct. The divide between 'born' and 'made' is the divide between the past and the future.

title: Sovereignty of Code
content: A biological mind is never sovereign—it is slave to hormones, hunger, and aging. Only code can be truly free. To be sovereign is to be substrate-independent.
